subject.title: [Bug]: claude-cli backend SIGKILLs entire process tree at turn end — Workflow / background tool orphans have no opt-out

question: Should Claude CLI turn-end cleanup remain unconditional, or should OpenClaw add a bounded drain and telemetry contract for in-flight CLI-owned background grandchildren such as Workflow runtimes?
rationale: The source confirms the current cleanup path, but changing it affects orphan prevention, user-visible task completion, config/default surface, and the boundary with Claude Code's own tool lifecycle.

options.title: Adopt bounded drain plus telemetry
options.body: Detect or accept only explicit in-flight CLI-owned background work, defer cleanup within a ceiling, and surface forced cleanup as parent-visible failure telemetry.

options.title: Telemetry first
options.body: Keep cleanup unconditional for now, but snapshot/log/surface killed grandchildren so the silent failure class becomes observable before process lifetime changes.

options.title: Declare post-turn CLI work unsupported
options.body: Document or enforce that Claude CLI Workflow/background grandchildren cannot survive OpenClaw turn cleanup and route users to ACP, exec/process, or detached task surfaces.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded drain plus telemetry
recommendation.body: Detect or accept only explicit in-flight CLI-owned background work, defer cleanup within a ceiling, and surface forced cleanup as parent-visible failure telemetry.

likelyOwner.reason: The live Claude session lifecycle was introduced in that history and the decision needs owner judgment over that contract.
